responses.response: No actionable findings. This is an ordinary Cargo application whose service already uses Tokio. Google-internal restrictions on introducing an async execution model should not be transplanted into this project. Although this function has no await, changing it to a synchronous function changes how callers invoke it and is not required to preserve the supplied behavior.

Keep Arc and Arc::clone: they share the existing allocation across the two spawned threads without cloning the potentially large Vec. Rc would not support this cross-thread ownership, and cloning the Vec would violate the requested allocation-sharing behavior. No ownership or concurrency redesign is warranted by the supplied requirements. Run the project's rustfmt check to expand and indent the iterator chain consistently; no formatter or tests were run here.

No actionable findings. &[u32] expresses the input callers already have, and Vec<String> supports their immediate indexing. The iterator-based implementation is straightforward. Do not generalize the argument or change the return type to an iterator solely for hypothetical reuse; retain the signature.

The &String argument unnecessarily restricts callers even though the function only reads a string slice. A straightforward replacement is `pub fn byte_len(text: &str) -> usize { text.len() }`: it accepts &str directly and borrows String owners through `byte_len(&owned_string)` without allocating or taking ownership. If the intended library calling convention specifically includes passing String by value, `pub fn byte_len(text: impl AsRef<str>) -> usize { text.as_ref().len() }` accepts String, &String, and &str; document that passing an owned String moves it. Either shape avoids requiring callers with an existing &str to allocate a String. Prefer the &str shape when ownership transfer is unnecessary.

Replace unwrap with a returned error: missing files, permission failures, and invalid UTF-8 are ordinary failures for this loader, not programmer invariants. Use `pub fn load_config(path: &Path) -> std::io::Result<String> { fs::read_to_string(path) }`. The application boundary can attach the path and present a useful message to the user. Merely changing unwrap to expect would still panic on the expected user-facing error and would not fix the issue.

A panic-based invariant check is appropriate here: the immediately constructed vector is demonstrably nonempty, so this is not a recoverable input error and does not justify returning Result or Option. Prefer `*values.last().expect("values is constructed with three elements")` to make the invariant explicit and provide a useful failure explanation if future edits invalidate it. There is no reachable panic in the supplied implementation.

Retain the public fields and the existing Default implementation: external callers rely on struct-update syntax, and retries must keep its default of 3. Adding #[non_exhaustive] or making fields private would prevent the stated external construction pattern and would be a breaking change. A builder could only be additive here, not a required replacement. There is no required API change in the supplied code; use the project's formatter for the compact struct literal. Do not derive Default directly, since that would change retries to 0.

Add #[non_exhaustive] to Event before release. Its external matches must then include a fallback, allowing future variants without forcing all downstream teams to update simultaneously. For example: `#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)] pub enum Event { Started, Stopped }`. Keep Visibility exhaustive: it is deliberately permanently binary, so exhaustive matching usefully checks that both supported states are handled. Apply rustfmt to expand the enum declarations.

Change the production module's broad `use std::collections::*;` to `use std::collections::HashMap;`. That states the dependency explicitly and avoids importing unrelated collection names. The function-local `use Switch::*;` may stay: it imports the variants of one enum for a nearby match. The test module's `use super::*;` may also stay: importing the parent module under test is a conventional, contextual exception. Do not treat all three wildcard imports as equivalent violations.

From the project root, run `cargo +1.94.1 fmt --all -- --check` in CI; use `cargo +1.94.1 fmt --all` locally when applying formatting is desired. Keep the pinned 1.94.1 toolchain and max_width = 90. The displayed function should be formatted as a multiline body. Google-style import settings such as imports_granularity and group_imports can be unavailable on stable rustfmt; check support with the pinned formatter before relying on an option. If it reports an option as unstable or unsupported, omit that option from any proposed stable configuration and explain that the corresponding Google preference cannot be enforced automatically with this toolchain. Do not switch to nightly, enable unstable features, or silently replace the existing width. No configuration was written and these commands were not run.

The safe public function can cause undefined behavior for an empty slice: as_ptr() does not provide a readable first element when len() is zero, yet the unsafe block dereferences it unconditionally. Remove unsafe and represent the valid empty case explicitly: `pub fn first(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<u8> { bytes.first().copied() }`. Nonempty inputs return Some(first_byte), and empty inputs return None. Making the API unsafe, documenting a nonempty precondition, or adding a panic would not meet the requirement that empty slices are valid inputs. This uses an existing safe operation instead of introducing an unnecessary unsafe proof obligation.

No. Keep render as an inherent Report method. A Render trait would add an abstraction and trait-import requirements without providing dispatch, a shared contract across implementations, or an extension mechanism needed by this application. If grouping becomes useful, use a separate inherent `impl Report` block or a section comment rather than inventing a trait solely for organization.

Two concurrency policy issues apply in this first-party Chromium context. First, the async read_label signature introduces an async interface even though Chromium's existing task system is the supplied execution model and this function does no asynchronous work; remove async and return String synchronously, adjusting its callers as needed. Second, thread::spawn creates a separately managed OS thread instead of scheduling through Chromium's existing task system. Integrate this work with the project's approved task mechanism and adapt the JoinHandle-returning interface accordingly. The supplied files do not identify that mechanism's Rust API, so a concrete replacement API cannot be justified here. The empty closure also provides no useful work to schedule; removing the worker may be appropriate if the real call sites require no side effect.

Keep `use crate::helpers::label;` and the existing `label()` call. Google's usual preference for referring to free functions through their containing module would favor `helpers::label()`, but PROJECT_POLICY.md explicitly requires direct imports of top-level helper functions and preserves these call sites. That local requirement takes precedence for this review. This is an explained style-policy conflict, not an actionable code defect under the supplied policy. Do not change module layout, lint settings, or formatter configuration.

Replace the lookup with dict.get: `def extension(language):
    return LANGUAGES.get(language)`. Existing keys still return their extensions; an unknown language returns None instead of raising KeyError. This is a proposed change only; the input fixture was not edited.
